exact_statement_tex: \label{thm:finite-descent} Let $A$ be a semilocal noetherian ring, $\mathfrak m=\operatorname{rad}A$, and $A'$ a finite $A$-algebra. Put $A_n=A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$, $A'_n=A'\otimes_AA_n$, and \[ B=H^0(A'/A),\qquad B^{(n)}=H^0(A'_n/A_n), \] where $H^0$ is the equalizer of the two maps to the tensor square. For any fixed integer $r\geq1$, the following three conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*] \item $H^1(A'_n/A_n,\mathbf G_a)=0$ for every $n$; \item $H^1(A'_n/A_n,\GL_r)=\{1\}$ for every $n$; \item $\Spec A'_n\to\Spec B^{(n)}$ is effective descent for all flat quasi-coherent modules for every $n$. \end{enumerate} Here $H^1$ denotes Amitsur cohomology, or its matrix-cocycle pointed set. If these conditions hold, then they hold for every finite $r$; moreover \[ H^1(A'/A,\mathbf G_a)=0,\qquad H^1(A'/A,\GL_r)=\{1\}\quad(r\geq1), \] and $\Spec A'\to\Spec B$ is effective descent for finite flat modules. If $A$ is Artinian, this map and its base change by every flat $B$-scheme are effective descent for all flat quasi-coherent modules, with no bound on rank.

There is an invertible module $P$ such that \begin{equation}\label{eq:deformed-torsor-graded} F_i/F_{i-1}\simeq L^{\otimes i}\otimes P^{\otimes i} \quad(0\leq i<p),\qquad P^{\otimes p}\simeq\OO_X,\qquad P|_{Z(s)}\simeq\OO_{Z(s)}. \end{equation} Here $Z(s)$ is the scheme-theoretic zero subscheme. The filtration is intrinsic to the given torsor action.

exact_statement_tex: \label{cor:normalized-equality-euler} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:genus-zero-equality-defect} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral very ample divisor, and let $M\ne\OO_X$ have order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Suppose $2g(Y)-2=pY^2$, and let $\pi:N\to X$ be the normalization of its chosen $\mu_p$-torsor. Choose a ruling presentation $k(N)=k(C)(t)$ as in Corollary~\ref{cor:very-ample-equality-almost-ruled}, and suppose $g(C)=0$. Let $r:S\to N$ be the proper birational morphism from a point-blowup model of $C\times\PP^1$ supplied by Proposition~\ref{prop:distinguished-ruled-cover}. Put \[ \mathcal T=R^1r_*\OO_S,\qquad \epsilon=\dim_kH^0(N,\mathcal T),\qquad d=Y^2. \] Then $\mathcal T$ has finite support and \begin{equation}\label{eq:genus-zero-equality-defect} H^1(N,\OO_N)=0,\qquad H^2(N,\OO_N)\simeq H^0(N,\mathcal T),\qquad \chi(\OO_N)=1+\epsilon. \end{equation} If $p\ne3$, then $\epsilon\equiv-1\pmod p$ and $\epsilon\geq p-1$. In particular $N$ has a nonrational singularity outside $D=\pi^*Y$, and the distinguished rational map $N\dashrightarrow C$ does not extend to a morphism. If $p=3$, write $d=2e$. Then $\epsilon\equiv-e-1\pmod3$. Rational singularities, or extension of that rational map, can occur only if $d\equiv4\pmod6$.

exact_statement_tex: \label{rem:characteristic-two-ample-residual} Suppose that $Y$ is merely ample, with the same characteristic-two equality and torsion hypotheses, and additionally suppose that $X$ has a purely inseparable ruled rational cover of degree two. If the resulting ruling curve $C$ has positive genus, the proof above still gives \[ g(C)=1,\qquad \chi(\OO_X)=K_X^2=c_2(X)=0,\qquad b_1(X)=b_2(X)=2. \] The general-fibre identities give a positive even integer $b=Y\cdot F$. Equation~\eqref{eq:characteristic-two-canonical-square}, before its strict inequality, then forces $b=2$ and $p_a(F)=1$. Moreover, $Y\to B=C^{(2)}$ is separable of degree two. Its degree is $Y\cdot F=2$; if it were inseparable, it would be a relative Frobenius followed by an isomorphism and would preserve genus. That would give $g(Y)=1$, contrary to $g(Y)=Y^2+1\geq2$. Thus the purely inseparable multisection obstruction in Proposition~\ref{prop:quasielliptic-multisection} does not already exclude this configuration. The genus-zero branch for merely ample $Y$ satisfies the necessary numerical conditions in Proposition~\ref{prop:rational-normalization-canonical}. The present proposition concerns the function field of the normalized cover and does not extend a chosen rational ruling map over every point of that cover. It supplies no existence example for the Picard kernel, and does not settle the higher-conductor or strict-inequality cases.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:rational-normalization-canonical} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor, and let $M\ne\OO_X$ have order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Suppose \[ 2g(Y)-2=pY^2, \] and let $\pi:N\to X$ be the normalization of the $\mu_p$-torsor defined by a trivialization of $M^{\otimes p}$. Assume that $N$ is birationally rational, and put $d=Y^2$. Choose a proper birational morphism $r:S\to N$, where $S$ is obtained from $\PP^1\times\PP^1$ by finitely many point blowups, and put \[ \mathcal T=R^1r_*\OO_S,\qquad \epsilon=\dim_k H^0(N,\mathcal T). \] Then $\mathcal T$ has finite support and \begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-normalization-canonical-cohomology} \begin{gathered} H^1(N,\OO_N)=0,\qquad H^2(N,\OO_N)\simeq H^0(N,\mathcal T),\\ \chi(\OO_N)=1+\epsilon,\qquad \epsilon\in\{0,1\}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} If $\epsilon=1$, then \[ \omega_N\simeq\OO_N,\qquad \bigl(\omega_X(-(p-1)Y)\bigr)^{\otimes p}\simeq\OO_X,\qquad K_X\equiv(p-1)Y. \] In particular: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item No such birationally rational normalization exists for $p\geq5$. \item If $p=2$, then $\epsilon=1$ and \[ \begin{gathered} \chi(\OO_X)=1,\qquad K_X\equiv Y,\qquad 1\leq d=K_X^2\leq9,\\ b_1(X)=0,\qquad b_2(X)=10-d. \end{gathered} \] \end{enumerate} Here $b_i$ denotes the dimension of $\ell$-adic cohomology for any prime $\ell\ne p$.

exact_statement_tex: \label{rem:rational-canonical-scope} The strict characteristic-two inequality concerns smooth very ample divisors and the smallest equality. It does not exclude a torsion class satisfying a strict inequality or a higher conductor equality. For merely ample $Y$ in characteristic two, Proposition~\ref{prop:rational-normalization-canonical} gives a necessary numerical package, with no contradiction claimed. In every characteristic, the proposition assumes that the distinguished normalization is birationally rational. Thus its exclusion for $p\geq5$ does not exclude a ruling with positive-genus base. In characteristic three, the rational-normalization case with $\epsilon=0$ and $Y^2\equiv4\pmod6$, as well as the positive-genus case, remains unresolved here. The argument imposes no rational-double-point hypothesis on $N$: when $\epsilon=1$, its nonzero higher-direct-image defect expressly witnesses a nonrational singularity.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:normalized-mup-conductor} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth ample integral curve, and let $M$ be a nontrivial line bundle of order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Choose a trivialization of $M^p$ and let $T\to X$ be its $\mu_p$-torsor. Let $N$ be the normalization of $T$ and $\pi:N\to X$ the resulting finite map. The logarithmic differential of $M$ has order $pa$ along $Y$ for an integer $a\geq1$, with nonzero tangential leading coefficient. The full inverse image $D=\pi^*Y$ is a reduced integral ample Cartier divisor. At its generic point the ramification index is one, the residue degree is $p$, and the conductor of $T$ in $N$ has coefficient $a(p-1)$. The normalization $\widetilde D$ of $D$ has genus $g(Y)$. Let $\mathfrak c\subset\OO_N$ be the conductor ideal, put $c=a(p-1)$, and set $\mathcal J=\mathfrak c\otimes\OO_N(cD)$. Then $\mathcal J$ is a reflexive ideal in $\OO_N$, and its restriction embeds in $\OO_D$ with finite-length quotient. Write $\ell$ for that length and put $\delta=p_a(D)-g(Y)$. Without any smoothness or Gorenstein assumption on $N$, one has \[ 2g(Y)-2=ap\,Y^2+\frac{\ell+2\delta}{p-1}, \qquad \ell\geq0,\quad\delta\geq0. \] If $2g(Y)-2=ap\,Y^2$, then $D$ is smooth, $N$ is regular near $D$, $\mathcal J=\OO_N$, and $N$ is Gorenstein. exact_statement_tex: [Bounds for the Jacobian factor obstruction]\label{thm:scalar} Over every algebraically closed field, in every characteristic, an abelian variety of dimension $g>0$ satisfies \[ s_J(A)\mid(2g-1)!. \] If $g\leq3$, it also satisfies $s_J(A)\mid\delta(A)$. More precisely, \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \dim A&\text{bound}\\\hline 2&s_J(A)\mid\gcd(2,\delta(A))\\ 3&s_J(A)\mid\gcd(6,\delta(A)). \end{array} \] Consequently an abelian surface with an ample line bundle of odd Euler characteristic is a direct factor of a product of Jacobians. The same holds for a threefold if its ample Euler characteristics have greatest common divisor prime to six.

exact_statement_tex: [Identification with Milne's protorus]\label{prop:identification} Let \[ W=\varinjlim_{n\mid n'}W(p^n),\qquad a\longmapsto a^{n'/n}, \] be the group of Weil-number germs, using the full Weil-number definition of Milne \cite[Definition~2.5(a),(b), corrected author p.~13]{Milne1994}, including integrality after multiplication by a power of $p$. This is the character group of the finite-level protori in \cite[equation~(26), p.~23]{Milne2003}. The maps \[ [a,n]\longmapsto[a^{1/n}],\qquad W\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma/\mu_\infty \] are well defined and Galois equivariant. Consequently Milne's $P=D(W)$ is canonically $H^0\times\Gm$, and his weight-zero factor $P_0$ is $H^0$.
